THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 06.08.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.R.P.No.3880/2006  2  2025:KER:58716  ORDER
This revision petition has been filed challenging the judgment of acquittal.
2. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner reported no instructions.
Hence, notice was issued to the revision petitioner.
Though she received the notice, there is no appearance.
She has also not engaged any counsel as well.
Hence, I perused the records and heard the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
3. The revision petitioner is the defacto complainant and the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are the 1 st and 2nd accused in C.C.No.19/2004.
The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 498A, 494 and 406 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

The prosecution case in short is that, the 1 st accused,
suppressing the fact of his first marriage, married the daughter of the revision petitioner on the specific understanding that the properties owned by him situated at Ernakulam and Kannur would be transferred in her favour at his own expense for her maintenance and an agreement was executed to that effect.
It is alleged that thereafter, the 1st accused failed to execute the assignment deed as agreed.
It is further alleged that the 1 st 2025:KER:58716 accused demanded 2,00,000/- towards dowry and physically and mentally harassed the daughter of the petitioner.
It is also alleged that the 1st accused took away 75 sovereign of gold ornaments given to her at the time of the marriage.
It is also the case of the prosecution that the 2 nd and 3rd accused manhandled and criminally intimidated the daughter of the petitioner.
The 1 st and 2nd accused alone faced trial.
4. Before the trial court, PW1 to PW8 were examined and Exts.P1 to P5 were marked on the side of the prosecution.
After trial, the trial court found that the prosecution had failed to prove that the 1 st and 2nd accused committed the offences alleged.
Accordingly, they were acquitted.
5. PW1 is the revision petitioner.
She is the 1 st informant.
PW2 is the victim.
PW3 is the sister of PW2 and PW4 is a cousin of PW1.
Their evidence were relied on by the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused.
The trial court after evaluating their evidence found that the allegation of physical and mental harassment levelled against the 1 st accused is of a vague and general nature.
The trial court found that their oral evidence cannot be safely acted upon.

So far as the allegations regarding the misappropriation of gold ornaments and demand of dowry are concerned, the trial Kuttibi P.V vs P.H.Muhammad Ibrahim on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96223088/
2 court after evaluating the evidence on record 2025:KER:58716 found that the prosecution had not succeeded in proving the same.

sentences.text: 6. In the case of acquittal, there is double presumption in favour of the accused.

Firstly, the presumption of innocence available to him under the fundamental principles of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law.
Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the order of the acquittal recorded by the court.

It is settled that only in exceptional cases where there are compelling circumstances and the judgment of acquittal is found to be perverse, the appellate court/revisional court can interfere with the order of acquittal.
I have carefully gone through the entire records, evidence, proceedings and the impugned judgment.
I find no impropriety or illegality therein warranting interference under the exercise of revisional powers vested with this court.
The criminal revision petition fails, and it is accordingly dismissed.
